The disk filled up and took the api down: at 03:14:00 Postgres failed with "No space left on device", the api aborted its transaction, shut down its worker pool and exited with status 1 at 03:14:06. It never came back in this log; the proxy logs "upstream api refused connection" every two minutes from 03:16 through to the end of the file at 05:30, while web and proxy kept serving normally.

The cause is the `report-export` job, which started at 03:05:00 and wrote a 512 MB CSV to `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/` every 12 seconds, 40 files (about 20 GB) by 03:12:48. The disk warnings follow it directly: 91% at 03:09:03, 99% at 03:13:30, then the db error 30 seconds later. The job's lines stop at 03:12:48, with no completion or failure message.

To recover, clear out `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/part-*.csv`, then start the api and confirm the db is healthy. Before the export runs again, it needs a size cap or a different volume from the database, since it shares the db's disk.

The log entries are dated 2026-03-09, not last night, so check this is the right file for the outage you mean. The periodic `cache: slow command` warnings run throughout the log from 02:00 and look unrelated.
